h1:
Chonburi in a Day Trip
Bang Saen Beach from Bangkok
intro: Chonburi is the closest stretch of sea to Bangkok that you can do as an easy out-and-back in one day. Bang Saen Beach sits about 100 kilometres from Bangkok, roughly 1.5 to 2 hours by motorway. This plan has you leaving early, swimming mid-morning, climbing Khao Sam Muk for the view, eating seafood by the sea in the afternoon, then stopping at Nong Mon Market for souvenirs before heading back — home before it gets late, no overnight stay needed.

blocks.html: If you only have one day off but you want to see the sea, Chonburi is the easiest answer for anyone in Bangkok. No need to take leave, no need to book a room — just wake up a little early and you get a full day out. This plan is built around places people actually go and food you can actually find, using Bang Saen Beach as the base and branching out to Khao Sam Muk and Ang Sila nearby.

blocks.text: Before You Go — What to Know

items: Distance — Bangkok to Bang Saen is about 100 km, roughly 1.5–2 hours on the motorway (Motorway No. 7) if traffic is clear
Leave early — Head out of Bangkok before 7am to dodge the inbound rush and reach Bang Saen by mid-morning
Weekdays beat weekends — Saturdays, Sundays and long holidays get crowded and parking is tight. If you can pick, a weekday is far more relaxed

No car? — You can take a van or coach from Mo Chit or Ekkamai to Chonburi, then a songthaew or motorbike taxi down to the beach. But if you want to hit several spots in one day, your own car is by far the easiest

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.title: Leave Bangkok → Arrive at Bang Saen Beach

items.activity: Leave Bangkok, get on Motorway No. 7 heading toward Chonburi
items.note: You can stop at a petrol station for coffee on the way — this stretch usually flows well

items.activity: Arrive at Bang Saen Beach, find parking along the beachfront road
items.note: The morning sun is still gentle, parking is open, and the beachfront is easy to stroll

items.activity: Walk the beach, rent a deck chair and sit by the sea
items.note: Deck chairs rent for around 30–50 THB each, usually bundled with ordering food from the chair vendor's stall

blocks.html: Bang Saen is a long sandy beach that people from Chonburi and Bangkok have come to for ages. The water may not be as clear as the southern seas, but you get that beach feeling without a long drive. A row of food stalls lines the sand — fried mussel pancakes, som tam, grilled chicken, and fresh grilled seafood — and you can order it all to eat right there on a deck chair.

items.activity: Drive up Khao Sam Muk, pay respects at the Chao Mae Sam Muk shrine and take in the sea view from the lookout
items.note: It's a public viewpoint with no entry fee. There are lots of wild monkeys, so stow everything in the car and don't walk around holding food bags in plain sight

items.activity: Stop for photos at the white-letter tunnel and the seaside viewing balcony near Khao Sam Muk
items.note: A popular check-in spot — fewer people before noon and the photos come out nicely

items.activity: Head back down for a swim at Bang Saen Beach before lunch
items.note: If you're going in the water, bring a change of clothes and a waterproof pouch for your phone

blocks.title: About the Khao Sam Muk monkeys
blocks.html: The monkeys at Khao Sam Muk are numerous and some are fairly aggressive. Don't feed them by hand, don't hold eye contact for long, and don't leave bags or plastic sacks lying around — they'll grab them in a flash. Roll your windows all the way up before getting out of the car, every time.

items.activity: Lunch at a seaside seafood restaurant around Laem Taen or Ang Sila
items.note: This zone has plenty of seafood spots right on the water — fresh ingredients, mid-range prices. Order sea bass, prawns and clams to taste

items.activity: Walk Ang Sila Market, check out the famous Ang Sila stone mortars and the dried seafood
items.note: Ang Sila is an old fishing community known for processed-seafood souvenirs and the stone mortars made locally

items.activity: Settle into a seaside café for coffee and shade in the afternoon
items.note: The Bang Saen–Khao Sam Muk area has several cafés with sea views — a good place to rest before moving on

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Chonburi trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Chonburi
items.note: Out and back in a day

items.name: Beachside fried mussels & hoy jor
items.blurb: The classic snack paired with Bang Saen Beach — crispy-battered fried mussels and fresh oysters, ordered straight to your deck chair by the sea. It's a casual bite you can find all along the beach.

items.name: Sea bass fried with fish sauce / steamed with lime
items.blurb: The staple seafood dish at the seaside restaurants around Laem Taen and Ang Sila. Fresh, firm fish — order it fried with fish sauce or steamed with lime, both perfect with hot steamed rice.

items.name: Grilled prawns / blanched cockles
items.blurb: Simple seafood where you can judge the freshness on the spot. Big grilled prawns dipped in a punchy seafood sauce — a plate that lots of tables order alongside the fish.

items.name: Nong Mon sticky rice in bamboo (khao lam)
items.blurb: The signature treat of Nong Mon Market — sweet coconut sticky rice roasted inside a bamboo tube, fragrant with coconut milk. Easy to take home as a souvenir and it keeps for several days.

items.name: Khanom jak
items.blurb: A Thai sweet wrapped in nipa-palm leaf and grilled until fragrant, filled with a sweet, rich coconut-flour filling. It's long been both a snack and a souvenir tied to Nong Mon Market — find it fresh in the market.

items.name: Processed seafood
items.blurb: Chili-topped pounded squid, fish ryukyu, dried prawns, shrimp paste, fish sauce — dry goods that travel home easily. Nong Mon Market has several vendors to choose from, and you can taste before you buy.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.title: Nong Mon Market → Back to Bangkok

items.activity: Stop at Nong Mon Market for khao lam, khanom jak and processed seafood to take home
items.note: Nong Mon Market is Chonburi's main souvenir hub, open morning to evening. It sits right on Sukhumvit Road on the way back to Bangkok
The evening return on a holiday can get busy heading into the city, so leave a little buffer

items.activity: Arrive in Bangkok, wrapping up the one-day beach trip
items.note: Leave around this time and you'll be home before dark, not too worn out

blocks.text: Tweak the Plan for Who You're With

items.name: With kids / family
items.blurb: Focus on swimming at Bang Saen Beach, cut the time on Khao Sam Muk since the monkeys can be scary for little ones, then finish with khao lam from Nong Mon Market.

items.name: Seafood lovers
items.blurb: Skip the swim and head straight to the seafood restaurants at Laem Taen–Ang Sila from noon, then keep walking Ang Sila Market to browse the dried seafood.

items.name: Photo / café crowd
items.blurb: Focus on the Khao Sam Muk viewpoint, the white-letter tunnel, and the sea-view cafés. Go in the morning for nicer light and fewer people.

faq.q: Can you really do Chonburi as a day trip from Bangkok?
faq.a: Easily. Bang Saen is about 100 km from Bangkok, roughly 1.5–2 hours by motorway. Leave around 6–7am and you'll arrive by mid-morning — swim, climb Khao Sam Muk, eat seafood, and be back in Bangkok before evening.

faq.q: No car — how do I get to Bang Saen?
faq.a: You can take a van or coach from Mo Chit or Ekkamai to Chonburi/Bang Saen, then a songthaew or motorbike taxi down to the beach. But if you also want to hit several spots in one day, like Khao Sam Muk and Ang Sila, your own car is much more convenient.

faq.q: Should I go on a weekday or a weekend?
faq.a: A weekday is far more relaxed — fewer people and easy parking. Saturdays, Sundays and long holidays get very crowded, traffic builds up and parking fills fast. If you can choose, go on a weekday.

faq.q: Where's the best place to buy Chonburi souvenirs?
faq.a: Nong Mon Market is the main souvenir hub, right on Sukhumvit Road along the route back to Bangkok. The signature buys are khao lam, khanom jak, and processed seafood like chili-topped pounded squid, fish ryukyu, and dried prawns.

faq.q: Is Khao Sam Muk dangerous because of the monkeys?
faq.a: The monkeys at Khao Sam Muk are numerous and some are fairly aggressive. Roll your car windows all the way up, don't walk around holding food bags, don't hold eye contact for long, and keep valuables out of sight. Stay alert and you'll be fine.
